MOLECULAR PATHOLOGY REPORT
[redacted location] Cancer Center

PATIENT: [redacted name]
MRN: [redacted ID]
DOB: [redacted date]
AGE/SEX: 59-year-old male
SPECIMEN: Lung biopsy tissue
DATE COLLECTED: [redacted date]
DATE RECEIVED: [redacted date]
DATE REPORTED: [redacted date]

CLINICAL HISTORY
Metastatic lung adenocarcinoma. Previous molecular testing negative for EGFR, KRAS, and BRAF mutations. ALK rearrangement testing negative.

TEST PERFORMED
ROS1 Gene Rearrangement Analysis by Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH)

METHODOLOGY
Interphase FISH analysis was performed on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded lung biopsy tissue sections using the GeneSight ROS1 Dual Color Break Apart Probe (MolecularProbe R-2100). This probe set consists of a green fluorophore labeling the 5' (centromeric) region of ROS1 and an orange fluorophore labeling the 3' (telomeric) region of ROS1 at chromosome 6q22. A minimum of 100 tumor cell nuclei were evaluated.

RESULTS
ROS1 (6q22) FISH: ABNORMAL - Inconclusive for ROS1 rearrangement

Signal Pattern Analysis:
- Normal pattern (2 fusion signals): 42%
- Abnormal pattern with additional 5'ROS1 signal: 58%
- Classic break-apart pattern: 0%

The predominant abnormal signal pattern shows an additional copy of the centromeric 5'ROS1 (green) signal without corresponding 3'ROS1 (orange) signal or classic separation of probe signals.

INTERPRETATION
The FISH analysis reveals an abnormal signal pattern characterized by an additional copy of the centromeric 5'ROS1 probe signal. This pattern may indicate either:
1. ROS1 rearrangement with subsequent loss of the derivative chromosome containing the 3'ROS1 fusion partner
2. Deletion involving 6q22 without true ROS1 fusion

The absence of classic break-apart signals makes this result inconclusive for determining the presence of a therapeutically targetable ROS1 rearrangement. The clinical and therapeutic significance of this abnormal signal pattern remains unclear.

RECOMMENDATIONS
ROS1 immunohistochemistry (IHC) is recommended to further define ROS1 status. Positive ROS1 protein expression by IHC would support the presence of a ROS1 rearrangement, while negative staining would suggest the abnormal FISH pattern is not associated with a functional ROS1 fusion protein.
